topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: According to the NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual's 'Preparing To Ride' section, what is the first of the four things a safe rider does before any trip?
explanation: The manual lists four steps a safe rider takes before any trip, in order: (1) wear the right gear, (2) become familiar with the motorcycle, (3) check the motorcycle equipment, and (4) be a responsible rider.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Preparing To Ride' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: The NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual states that in any crash, you have a better chance to avoid serious injury if you wear which combination of gear?
choice_a: A helmet and a windshield only
choice_b: An approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothes
choice_d: A jacket, a helmet, and mirrors
explanation: The manual specifically lists three elements of 'the right gear': an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothes.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Wear The Right Gear' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: According to the manual, what proportion of motorcycle crashes results in head or neck injuries?
explanation: The manual states that one out of every five motorcycle crashes results in head or neck injuries, and that these injuries account for a majority of serious and fatal injuries to motorcyclists.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Use' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: A study cited in the manual examined more than 900 motorcycle crashes in which 40% of the riders wore helmets. What did the study find regarding helmets and a rider's ability to spot danger to the sides?
choice_a: It found helmets reduced side vision by nearly half
choice_b: It found helmeted riders spotted danger significantly slower
choice_c: It found no motorcyclists wore helmets during the study period
choice_d: It did not find even one case in which a helmet kept a rider from spotting danger
explanation: Some riders avoid helmets because they believe helmets limit peripheral vision, but the manual cites a study of over 900 crashes (40% of riders helmeted) that did not find even one case where a helmet kept a rider from spotting danger.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Use' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: Per the manual, most motorcycle crashes happen under which circumstance?
choice_a: On short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after starting out
choice_b: On trips longer than 50 miles after hours of riding
choice_c: While the motorcycle is parked or stationary
explanation: The manual notes most crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long, just a few minutes after starting out.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Use' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: According to the manual, at speeds under 30 mph, what effect can a helmet have on head injuries?
choice_b: It can cut both the number and the severity of head injuries by half
choice_c: It only reduces injury severity, not the number of injuries
choice_d: It increases the number of minor injuries reported
explanation: The manual states that most riders are going slower than 30 mph when a crash occurs, and at these speeds helmets can cut both the number and severity of head injuries by half.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Use' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: Regardless of crash speed, how much more likely are helmeted riders to survive head injuries compared to riders not wearing helmets, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states that no matter what the speed, helmeted riders are three times more likely to survive head injuries than those not wearing helmets at the time of the crash.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Use' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: The manual describes two primary types of helmets that provide different levels of coverage. What are they?
explanation: According to the 'Helmet Selection' section, there are two primary types of helmets providing two different levels of coverage: three-quarter and full face.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Selection' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: Which of the following reflects the manual's guidance for selecting a helmet?
choice_a: It should meet DOT and state standards (a Snell Memorial Foundation label adds assurance of quality), fit snugly all around, have no obvious defects such as cracks or frayed straps, and be kept securely fastened when riding
choice_b: It should be the lightest helmet available regardless of certification
choice_c: It only needs to fit loosely so it can be removed quickly
choice_d: Any helmet is acceptable as long as it has a chin strap
explanation: The manual advises choosing a helmet that meets DOT and state standards (a Snell Memorial Foundation label gives added assurance), fits snugly all around, has no obvious defects, and is kept securely fastened -- otherwise it is likely to fly off before it can protect you in a crash.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Helmet Selection' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the protection provided by a face shield, goggles, and a windshield, per the manual?
choice_a: Goggles protect the whole face better than a face shield does
choice_b: A plastic shatter-resistant face shield helps protect the whole face, while goggles protect only the eyes and a windshield is not a substitute for either
choice_c: A windshield fully replaces the need for a face shield or goggles
choice_d: All three provide identical eye and face protection
explanation: The manual explains a face shield helps protect the whole face, goggles protect the eyes but not the rest of the face, and a windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles since most windshields will not protect the eyes from wind.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Eye And Face Protection' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: Which of the following is listed among the requirements for effective eye or face protection, and when should tinted protection be avoided?
choice_a: It must be tinted at all times to reduce glare, even at night
choice_b: It only needs to fasten securely; scratches and fogging do not matter
choice_c: It must be free of scratches, resistant to penetration, give a clear view to either side, fasten securely, and permit air to pass through to reduce fog; tinted protection should not be worn at night or when little light is available
choice_d: It must block airflow completely to keep out dust
explanation: The manual lists five requirements for effective eye or face protection: free of scratches, resistant to penetration, a clear view to either side, fastens securely, and permits air to pass through to reduce fog. It also warns that tinted eye protection should not be worn at night or any other time when little light is available.
source_note: NYS DMV Motorcycle Manual, 'Eye And Face Protection' section

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: According to the 'Clothing' section, how should a jacket and pants fit, and what material offers the most protection?
choice_a: They should fit as loosely as possible for maximum airflow, and material choice does not affect protection
choice_b: They should be skin-tight for aerodynamics, and cotton offers the most protection
choice_c: A jacket is only necessary in cold weather and can be skipped when it's warm
choice_d: They should cover the arms and legs completely, fit snugly enough to avoid flapping but loosely enough to move freely, with leather offering the most protection; a jacket should be worn even in warm weather
explanation: The manual states jacket and pants should cover the arms and legs completely, fit snugly enough to keep from flapping yet loosely enough to move freely, with leather offering the most protection (sturdy synthetic material also provides a lot of protection); a jacket should be worn even in warm weather to prevent dehydration.

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: What does the manual recommend regarding boots or shoes for riding?
choice_a: They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support the ankles, have hard slip-resistant soles, short heels, and laces tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle
choice_b: Any low-top athletic shoe is acceptable as long as it is comfortable
choice_c: Tall heels are preferred because they improve foot control
choice_d: Loose, untied laces are fine since they won't affect riding
explanation: The manual advises boots or shoes should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support the ankles, with hard, durable slip-resistant soles, short heels so they don't catch on rough surfaces, and laces tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

topic: Protective Gear: Helmets, Eye Protection & Clothing
question: What does the manual say about gloves and about clothing needs in cold or wet weather?
choice_a: Gloves are optional and provide no crash protection benefit
choice_b: Gloves should be leather or similar durable material to allow a better grip and help protect the hands in a crash; in cold or wet weather, clothing should keep the rider warm and dry since riders cannot control a motorcycle well if they are numb
choice_c: Cold-weather gear is unnecessary as long as the rider wears a helmet
choice_d: Wet-weather clothing should prioritize style over keeping the rider dry
explanation: The manual states gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material to allow a better grip and protect the hands in a crash. In cold or wet weather, clothing should keep the rider warm and dry, since riding while numb makes it hard to control the motorcycle and long periods in cold weather can cause severe chill and fatigue.
